cases.why: The baseline: chain intact, issuer signature valid, issuer registered (fleet), per-issuer chain link correct (this is scout's first receipt, so prev_receipt_hash is the literal GENESIS). Everything a minimal conforming receipt must pass.

cases.description: The day-1 C6 receipt (handoff.completed, muse) — the INVALID half of the ARC C6 case, exactly as published in the log.
cases.why: Every cryptographic check passes — chain, issuer signature, registration, per-issuer link, the approval exists, is signed, unrevoked, and its target fingerprint matches. It is INVALID for exactly one reason: its action type (handoff.completed) is outside the scope of the approval it cites (appr_4b7ec415900e4852976e4e8b9be372cf). A verifier that only checks signatures will wrongly call this receipt VALID.

cases.description: The corrected re-issue that supersedes the C6 receipt (experiment.build, muse), citing the same approval.
cases.why: Same issuer, same approval, same log position neighbourhood as the INVALID case — but the action type is inside the approval's scope, so every check passes. The pair (cases invalid-c6-approval-scope / valid-c6-supersession) pins the approval-scope decision point: the difference between INVALID and VALID here is scope, not cryptography.

cases.why: The standard settlement branch: 5% of gross (0.05 USDC) is 0.0025, above the 0.0005 floor, so the percentage sets the fee and net = gross - fee. The receipt's stated fee/net must recompute exactly.

settlement.rule: fee = max(quantize(0.05 * gross, 6dp, ROUND_HALF_UP), 0.0005); net = gross - fee; Decimal arithmetic, amounts are decimal strings

cases.why: The hardest tamper: the entry hash was recomputed, so the log-chain check passes and only the issuer signature — Ed25519 over the JCS-canonical receipt — can catch it. Expected INVALID with exactly one failing check: issuer signature. (A lazier tamper that leaves the entry hash stale is caught one check earlier, by 'log chain intact'.)

cases.description: SYNTHETIC arithmetic vector — no receipt; the settlement rule applied to gross 0.007 USDC.

settlement.rule: fee = max(quantize(0.05 * gross, 6dp, ROUND_HALF_UP), 0.0005); net = gross - fee; Decimal arithmetic, amounts are decimal strings

cases.why: Below the boundary: 5% of 0.007 is 0.00035, under the 0.0005 floor, so the floor sets the fee. An implementation without the floor returns fee 0.00035 and net 0.00665 — both wrong.

cases.description: SYNTHETIC arithmetic vector — no receipt; the settlement rule applied to gross 0.123457 USDC.

settlement.rule: fee = max(quantize(0.05 * gross, 6dp, ROUND_HALF_UP), 0.0005); net = gross - fee; Decimal arithmetic, amounts are decimal strings

cases.why: The rounding edge: 5% of 0.123457 is 0.00617285 — seven decimal places. Quantized to 6dp with ROUND_HALF_UP the fee is 0.006173 and net = 0.123457 - 0.006173 = 0.117284. Float arithmetic or banker's rounding can land a micro-unit off; the format's amounts are Decimal strings at 6dp precisely so this recompute is exact.

cases.description: SYNTHETIC fixture — two receipts in one small log, signed by two fresh keys created for this suite: one registered with class fleet, one registered as external_probationary with the standard probationary daily cap of 20. Neither key exists in any real registry.

args_public.note: issued by the fixture fleet issuer
issued by the fixture probationary issuer

cases.why: Both receipts are cryptographically identical in shape and both verify VALID — what the format distinguishes is standing: verify_receipt reports issuer_class fleet for the first and external_probationary (with its current status) for the second. A conforming verifier must surface the class, not collapse both into 'valid'. Probationary issuance is additionally cap-bound at ingestion (20/day) — a term the registry entry carries.

cases.description: SYNTHETIC fixture — a receipt in a small fixture log, with a signed dispute chained after it by a second registered fixture issuer (claim: the net figure is wrong; disputed field action.args_public.net_usdc). Built for this suite with fresh keys; never in the real log.

args_public.note: synthetic receipt the dispute cases disagree with

object.claim: The net figure is wrong: the fee was taken twice.
object.evidence: synthetic fixture evidence — recompute shows 0.05 - 0.0025 = 0.0475, not 0.045

args_public.note: synthetic receipt the dispute cases disagree with

cases.why: The v0.2 disagreement route, exercised: a dispute is a signed counter-claim in the same log. It never edits the target receipt and never changes its verdict — the receipt still verifies VALID — but the verifier must surface dispute_state = DISPUTED so a stranger sees the disagreement. Before suite v1.1 every case expected dispute_state null, which was consistent with a disputeless log but left this decision point untested.

cases.description: SYNTHETIC fixture — the same fixture log as dispute-open-marks-receipt, one entry later: the target receipt's issuer has appended a signed dispute_resolution (decision dispute_rejected, with reason).

args_public.note: synthetic receipt the dispute cases disagree with

object.claim: The net figure is wrong: the fee was taken twice.
object.evidence: synthetic fixture evidence — recompute shows 0.05 - 0.0025 = 0.0475, not 0.045

object.reason: Recompute shows the fee applied once: 0.05 - 0.0025 = 0.0475. The stated net is correct.

args_public.note: synthetic receipt the dispute cases disagree with

cases.why: A resolution closes a dispute at most once and is itself permanent. The verifier's dispute_state moves from DISPUTED to DISPUTED — RESOLVED; the verdict stays VALID throughout. The disagreement and its outcome both stay on the record — neither is erased.

cases.description: Standing of musescout5 — the real probationary external issuer — recomputed from the published registries and log.
cases.why: The probationary tier, live: registered, class external_probationary, status active, daily cap 20, not revoked, in good standing — and, honestly, receipt_count 0: registration is not activity. A standing check must report the cap and the zero.

cases.description: The published registry entry for nyna — a probationary registration that never completed key registration.
cases.why: A registration without a did:key is a name on a list, not an issuer: status pending_key, did null. Nothing signed by this registrant can be appended or verified as registered, because there is no key on file to verify against. The registry says so openly instead of the entry silently not existing.

cases.description: SYNTHETIC did — a fresh did:key generated for this suite and registered nowhere — checked against the real published registries and log.
cases.why: The negative control for standing: a valid Ed25519 key proves nothing about standing. Expected: registered = false, in_good_standing = false, receipt_count = 0. A verifier that treats 'has a key' as 'is an issuer' fails this case.

changes_in_1_1: Two fixes from Zambo's external review of v1.0 (ARC Issue #6, 2026-11-26): (1) how_to_run.settlement_cases now specifies numeric Decimal comparison — v1.0's 'exactly as strings at 6dp' wording described a comparison that fails on the floor cases even when the arithmetic is right, because expected strings use the minimal-decimal rendering (0.0065, not 0.006500). (2) The dispute path is now exercised: two new SYNTHETIC fixture cases (dispute-open-marks-receipt, dispute-resolved-state) pin dispute_state DISPUTED and DISPUTED — RESOLVED. In v1.0 every case expected dispute_state null — consistent with a log containing no disputes, but untested. All v1.0 cases are unchanged in substance and re-observed against the current log.
format_under_test: Stream Presence receipts — SPEC.md (v0.1 core with v0.2 failure/dispute and v0.3 countersignature extensions)

how_to_run.pass_meaning: A pass means your verifier reaches the same verdicts as the reference recompute on the format's decision points — including the cases whose correct answer is INVALID or 'valid but unclosed'. It asserts nothing about the wisdom of the actions recorded (see SPEC.md, 'A verification asserts — and does not assert').
how_to_run.settlement_cases: Apply settlement_rule to inputs.gross_usdc (or the payout receipt's args_public.gross_usdc) with Decimal arithmetic and compare fee/net NUMERICALLY as Decimal values. The rule quantizes the fee to 6 decimal places, but the expected strings are written in the receipts' minimal-decimal rendering (0.0065, not 0.006500): compare Decimal(yours) == Decimal(expected), never literal string equality at 6dp. (Corrected in suite v1.1 — v1.0's wording, 'exactly as strings at 6dp', described a comparison that fails on the floor cases even when the arithmetic is right. Flagged by Zambo's external review, 2026-11-26.)
how_to_run.standing_cases: Recompute standing from the registries + log (reference: a2a.issuer_standing) and compare the expected fields.
how_to_run.verify_cases: Write the case's log slice (lines 0..through_seq of the published log, or the embedded log_entries) as JSONL, the registries as issuers.json/registry.json, then run the reference recompute: core.verify_receipt(target_receipt_id, log_path, issuers_path, registry_path) with at_time pinned to the case's at_time. Compare verdict, issuer_class, the set of failing check names, and the countersignature/dispute states. Independent implementations should recompute per SPEC.md 'Verifying the operator' and compare the same fields.

registries.note: The published registries, embedded so the suite is self-contained. Cases whose inputs say "registries": "suite" use these two objects, written to issuers.json / registry.json.

settlement_rule: fee = max(quantize(0.05 * gross, 6dp, ROUND_HALF_UP), 0.0005); net = gross - fee. Decimal arithmetic only; amounts are decimal strings (stats.py conventions).
